case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Mother
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the portion of the family court's order directing DSS to forego reunification efforts and file a TPR petition, finding the preponderance of the evidence supported returning the twins home with twelve months of DSS supervision and services.
key_cases.relevance: It is South Carolina's clearest appellate reaffirmation of reunification as the preferred outcome where the evidence supports it.
key_cases.quote: we find the family court erred in ordering SCDSS to initiate TPR proceedings against Mother

key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Hogan
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court reversed and remanded for a merits hearing, holding the family court had jurisdiction to order reunification and a merits hearing where no affirmative finding of abuse or neglect had ever been made, and condemning the practice of holding such findings in abeyance while children remain in foster care.
key_cases.relevance: The decision preserves the family court's power to order reunification where no adjudication has occurred.
key_cases.quote: We find this practice is in clear contravention of the removal statutes and could violate the fundamental right parents have to raise their children.

key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Briggs
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed removal of the infant based on abuse of the older siblings but reversed the permanent plan and the order relieving DSS of reasonable efforts, holding the family court failed to make the specific written findings § 63-7-1640(F) requires.
key_cases.relevance: Briggs protects reunification as the default plan absent adequate findings justifying its abandonment.
key_cases.quote: we reverse and remand for a new permanency planning hearing and for the family court to make specific written findings to support its decision as required by subsection 63-7-1640(F)

key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Cameron N.F.L.
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court reversed termination of the mother's parental rights, holding that even assuming a statutory ground existed, TPR was not in the child's best interest given the valuable bond between mother and child.
key_cases.relevance: Cameron N.F.L. preserves an existing parent-child bond as a reason to keep reunification or continued contact on the table.
key_cases.quote: we hold the family court erred in finding termination of Mother's parental rights was in Child's best interest

key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Sarah W.
key_cases.holding: The court upheld the 15-of-22-months ground as facially constitutional and reinstated termination, holding that the ground requires both a best-interests finding and that the delay in reunification be attributable to the parent rather than to the State.
key_cases.relevance: It requires courts to ask why reunification did not occur before treating elapsed foster care time as a reason to abandon it.
key_cases.quote: section 63-7-2570(8) may not be used to sever parental rights based solely on the fact that the child has spent fifteen of the past twenty-two months in foster care

key_cases.case_name: Charleston County Department of Social Services v. Marccuci
key_cases.holding: The court reversed termination of an incarcerated father's parental rights, holding DSS proved neither willful failure to visit nor willful failure to support and that the fifteen-of-twenty-two-months ground could not carry termination where the delay that kept the child in foster care was generated by continuances and agency road blocks rather than by the father.
key_cases.relevance: Marccuci is the South Carolina Supreme Court decision that reunification must remain the goal where the child stayed in foster care because of continuances and agency delay rather than parental failure, and the Court directed DSS to implement a reunification plan immediately on filing.
key_cases.quote: While the family court's determination is technically correct, the facts of this case militate against strict adherence to section 63-7-2570(8).
